title: Feature update
summary: Announce one new feature or release of a software product (what's new, changelog, release notes video), 10-45 s on the real screens: the change, before and after, and where to try it.

notFor.when: the film teaches how to do a whole task step by step (how to use the feature, onboarding, a walkthrough)
the film sells the whole product or launches the product itself (ad, promo, brand launch film), not one change to it

alternatives.when: the user already recorded the new feature on screen themselves and wants it cut, captioned and finished (cut mechanics: footage-edit)

qa: The new state is on screen within the first 3 s, before any title, logo or 'before' shot
Before and after are captured at the same viewport, scale and camera stop, so only the change moves between them
The version label, date and availability on screen match the release the user confirmed
The in-app cut reads completely with sound off: every claim is on-screen text or a burned caption
One change per film; a roundup gives each change its own result shot and no change gets a claim without its screen

intake.ask: What exactly changed, in one sentence, and how did the user do this before the release?
intake.why: The film is the before and after of one job; without the old way there is nothing to compare.

intake.ask: Where can the old and the new version run with seed data (staging URL, feature flag, previous build, local repo)?
intake.why: Before and after are two captures of the real product at the same framing.
intake.default: The new version from the URL given; the old state from the current production build, captured the same way

intake.ask: Which version label, release date and availability (plans, platforms, rollout) go on screen?
intake.why: A wrong version or a feature shown to users who do not have it is a false claim.

intake.ask: Where does it ship: LinkedIn, X, the product's site or changelog, an in-app modal, an email?
intake.why: Each placement sets the formats, the length and whether it plays muted.
intake.default: LinkedIn and X in landscape and square, plus a silent in-app cut

intake.ask: Where should the viewer go to try it (the in-product path, a deep link, an upgrade page)?
intake.why: The end card names one action and one place.
intake.default: The in-product path to the feature, spelled as it reads in the UI

intake.ask: Is this one feature, or a release with several changes that should share one film?
intake.why: One headline change gets its own film; several small ones become a roundup with a different method.
intake.default: One film for the headline change; the smaller ones listed on a closing card or left to the written changelog

profiles.note: LinkedIn recommends 15-30 s for every feed placement; under 30 s loops; captions as an SRT sidecar (captions:export).
X recommends 16:9 or 1:1 and plays 720p for non-Premium accounts: read UI larger. Length band is a house rule, starting point.
Site, changelog page and in-app modal play muted (Chrome allows muted autoplay only): build it to read silent. Band is a house rule, starting point.

starter.note: Read the real capture with ui-camera-read, carry the changed element from before to after, before-after-split only when the change is a number, a still end card with version and path.

variants.title: Release roundup
variants.changes: One to three headline changes, each its own result shot and before-after, then the small fixes as one fast list card. Over 45 s drop --profile promo (full profile). One version label and date for the release.

variants.title: In-app cut-down
variants.changes: 5-15 s (house rule), result and one before-after only, no voice, every claim as on-screen text, render with --captions on, square; the player starts it muted. Email gets a motion:still poster of the result linked to the hosted film.
